title: Scene Reconstruction Using Ubiquitous Wireless Signals via Diffusion Posterior Inference Over physics-Grounded Representations
abstract: arXiv:2610.22120v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Knowing the layout of the physical world matters for many applications, yet the sensors we rely on for it (e.g., cameras and LiDAR) can fail in darkness, in adverse weather, or behind walls. Wireless signals do not face these limitations: every link between a base station and a user is shaped by the buildings it passes, reflects from, or is blocked by, leaving information about the surrounding scene embedded in the wireless channel measured at the endpoints. However, mapping channel measurements to the environment is a severely ill-posed problem: a measurement records only the structures that interact with the transmitted electromagnetic waves along its propagation paths, and even these observations can often be explained by multiple plausible scenes. translated_title: 基于物理特性表示上的扩散后验推断，利用泛在无线信号进行场景重建
translated_abstract: 了解物理世界的布局对许多应用都至关重要，然而我们所依赖的传感器（如摄像头和激光雷达）在黑暗、恶劣天气或墙壁遮挡的情况下可能失效。无线信号则不受这些限制：基站与用户之间的每一条链路都会受到其穿过、反射自或被其阻挡的建筑物的影响，从而将周围场景的信息嵌入到在链路两端测得的无线信道中。然而，将信道测量映射到环境是一个严重的病态问题：一次测量仅记录了沿传播路径与发射电磁波发生相互作用的结构，而且即使是这些观测也往往可以由多个合理的场景来解释。因此，我们将无线场景重建表述为后验推断问题，并开发了一个包含两个互补阶段的分层框架来解决这一问题。无线基础模……
tldr: 该论文将无线场景重建表述为后验推断问题，提出一个基于物理特性表示、结合扩散模型的两阶段分层框架，从泛在的无线信道测量中重建周围环境的场景布局。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates wireless scene reconstruction as posterior inference and develops a hierarchical two-stage framework with physics-grounded representations and diffusion models to reconstruct environmental scenes from ubiquitous wireless channel measurements.
